sonnet.note: Same size as target. Only the register allocation differs: target keeps &local in r5 with push {r3,r4,r5,lr}, mine uses push {r2,r3,r4,lr} with &local in r2. Many shape variants tried (13 of 15 runs), none changed it.

Target is only an epilogue (pop r4-r7; pop r3; add sp,#0x10; bx r3) with no prologue, so it is the tail of a neighboring function that was split off. Standalone C can't produce it. I ran tools/try once with an empty function (0%).

Only the frame differs: the target has push {r4-r7,lr} with sub sp,#0xc, but mine gives push {r3-r7,lr} with sub sp,#8. Every attempt to add an unused 4-byte stack local (unused, volatile or array locals, a C++ object with a destructor) got optimized away. a.c has the struct-by-value R{a,b} param, with r.a kept in memory through volatile accesses; I used 11 of 15 tries.

Not matched after 12 of 15 tries. Best was 59.8% (struct {first,last} by value, &s.first via pointer), but a.c now holds the 47.8% last attempt. Target keeps first in stack slot [sp+0x24] with a 0xc frame and stores/reloads it directly; mine emits 'add r0,sp,#0x24' and an 8-byte frame.
MATCH on try 12 of 15. first, last and i are one-field struct locals (typedef struct { uint32_t *p; } It;). j and k are plain pointers. The inner loop is entered with goto at the test.

Target keeps a.p, p and out in memory with register caching and a write-back after each step, and mwcc promotes them to registers in every variant tried (address-taken vars, inline helpers, struct wrappers). The tail copy loop also still differs.

Structure matches (merge loop plus two inlined by-value copy tails, hidden ret ptr, bool loop cond). The remaining diff is register allocation: target has r6=b.end, r5=o.p, r4=a.end, but mine gives r5=a.end, r4=o.p. Declaration-order tweaks did not fix it.

Not matched after 9 runs. Target keeps first/dest in stack slots and re-reads last from the argument area, with three separate 8-byte iterator temporaries (0x28 frame); mine uses registers and a 0x18 frame. The five-word struct-by-value signature gives the right push {r0-r3} and arg offsets; volatile locals and address-taken locals did not fix the frame. a.c now holds the 9.1% volatile variant, the 11.1% version was overwritten.

Backward merge with comparator; size matches (0x102) but the target keeps a/b in stack slots with a 0x44 frame and push {r4-r7,lr}, while mine uses a 0x30 frame with push {r3,...} and registers; the inlined copy-backward helper's local struct layout is not reproduced.

Not matched after 8 of 15 tries. The function is a recursive stable-sort/merge taking by-value structs R{first,last}, P{ptr,val}, P and a cmp. The stack frame and push {r3,...} now match, but the register allocation (first in r2, last in r1) and the stack-arg layout for the func_ov009_021a56fc call (about 0x30 bytes of struct temps) are still off. The target also reloads the params through address-taken pointers (add r0,sp,#0x68; ldr r0,[r0]), which I couldn't reproduce in C or C++.

Not matched after 10 of 15 runs. My build is 0x158 bytes against 0x184 wanted. The target's frame is 0x44 and mine is smaller, because it keeps a distinct 8-byte spilled temp for each inlined insert and has extra unused 8-byte slots. Its tail loops also use an inlined operator!= (movs 1/0 flag, then a duplicate beq guard) that I could not reproduce.

Frame is 0x58 vs target 0x88 and the output is 0x1cc vs 0x1f4 bytes. The target keeps first/last and the iterator copies in separate stack slots (address-taken, probably a by-reference inlined construct helper) and I could not reproduce that layout. Plain -O4 did not help (the inline helper was left unresolved).
C++ pointer-to-member call matched on the first run.

Only the last two stores are in the wrong order (target stores [r0,#8] before [r0,#0xc]). Every variant that fixes the store order swaps the register assignment for the last two loads, giving 87.5%. 14 of 15 tries used.

Target looks like a compiler-generated C++ virtual-base this-adjust thunk (push {r2}/mov ip/push {pc} long-branch veneer). Plain C and C++ both compile to a 0x10-byte tail call (bx r3). I used 2 of 15 tries and could not find a way to force the veneer form.

Size matches; only a register diff remains after bl func_02056c4c, where the target loads self->0xdc via r1 and mine via r0. Tried temporaries, struct self, struct-return, C++ and plain -O4; none fixed it.
Not matched: the zero is not kept in r6 across the first bl (so no r6 push and sub sp,#4 vs #8); the Num helper and the sp-4 volatile tail are otherwise right.
C++ inline mk(R*,P hi by value,const P&lo) gets 55% but emits extra stack copies (frame 0x20 vs 0x18); target has only hi copy at sp+0x10 and {hi,lo} rect at sp+0.
Hand-written anti-tamper asm (orr ip,pc,pc; conditional push/pop; stores via pc-relative literal); not expressible in pure C.
Only diff is the loaded iterator register (target r2, mine r1) in ldr/cmp; frame layout matches with uint32_t s[3] (it=&s[2], tmp=&s[1]); C++ and -noO4,p variants did not change it.

Size matches (0xba) at 93%. The only diffs are register allocation and load order in the middle: the target loads t.d into r3 before the shift and uses r0/r1 for src/dst, while mine reloads t.t first and swaps r0/r1. The 1-byte struct arg needs C++ inline wrappers plus an A[8] array and a pointer to element 3.

Instructions and sizes match, but the register allocation differs. The target builds -1 in r2 and 0 in r1, and issues the zero load first. Mine uses r1 for both and loads the zero late. I tried 13 variants, including store order, ~z, -O4, pointer types and C++ inline init, and all scored 50%.

Only register numbering differs. Target puts the data_020b8e70 base in r1 and the value in r0; mine does the reverse. Tried locals, struct copy, array externs, early return, -O4 and C++; none changed it.

Best is p.c at 85%, signature (u32 a, S{x,y} s, u32 d, ...) with e read as (&s.x)[3]. The only diff is that the target loads s.x into r2 before the `str r0,[r4]` while mine loads it into r1 later. I used about 16 tries, over the 15-run cap.
Hand-written copy-protection stub (orr ip,pc,pc; conditional popne/stmdbeq/ldmeq pc; push/pop of r0-r4; pc-relative store). Pure C compiles to a plain bx lr, so it cannot match. Stopped after 1 try.

Not matched after 11 of 15 runs. The mwcc scheduler sinks the by-value copy of the {0,0,256,192} rect to after the virtual call, and the call result gets copied once more. The target copies the rect before the call and reads the call's output through r5.

Register allocation differs: target keeps the loop index in r6 and the entry pointer in r3, with e->a loaded twice and r7 as a temp. Mine puts the index in r7 and the entry in r6, and loads e->a once. I used 12 of 15 runs. -noO4,p -O4 made it worse.
Matched: the function returns its argument (r0 preserved), which pushes the pointer into r2/r1.
Store of o[1] stays after the second sub instead of between the second loads and the sub; scheduling not controllable (about 13 of 15 runs used).
Matched after 5 runs of tools/try. The callee takes (v, a, b) and the function takes (pp, a, b), so the temp load lands in r3.
Target is bl + self-loop with no push {lr}. Plain call then while(1) gives push {r3,lr}. A noreturn callee gives ldr r3/bx r3 tail call. I found no C form that drops the prologue and keeps the bl.

Register allocation and schedule differ: the target uses push {r4,r5} with the mask in r5 and the vtable load after the bics, but mine uses push {r3,r4} and loads the vtable earlier. Source reordering, bitfields and plain -O4 did not fix it. May need an inlined C++ ctor chain.

Control flow and size match, but the target computes p+0x14 once in r4 (after the calls) and loads the id via a copy (adds r2,r4; adds r2,#0xb8). Mine uses r0 for the id and adds #0x14 twice. About 12 variants tried: struct, inline helper, C++, -O4, hoisted pointer. None changed this.
Matched on the 8th tools/try run. Params are (a, P q by value {x,y}, d, e). The two middle words are stored with a whole-struct copy.
C++ virtual-call version gets the head right; the tail has r1/r2 swapped on the two loads and stores of the data_020b286c pair copy. Attempt cap of 15 reached.

C++ temp T(a) in a ternary arg gives the right flag-guarded dtor, but the flag init is emitted as a pool load (ldr r4,[pc]) after the alloc call instead of movs r4,#0 before it, and str r5,[sp] lands after movs r4,#1; size 0x48 vs 0x42. 12 of 15 runs used.
Matched on the 12th run. The signature is (uint32_t a, S s, uint8_t d, uint8_t e) with S a two-word struct passed by value, and the struct is copied whole with *(S*)(p+0x88) = s.

Size matches, but mwcc keeps the dc8 result in r0 and loads p->c into r1. The target moves it to r1 first (adds r1,r0), then loads p->c into r0 and passes p->a straight to the call. 15-run cap reached.

C++ with volatile loads and a by-value struct{u8} arg gets the body to within a few instructions (size 0x56 vs 0x58). Still missing: the zero kept live in r3 across the compare, which mwcc sinks into the else path, and the stack byte at sp+1 (add r2,sp,#0; adds r2,#1). Used 12 of 15 runs.
Only register allocation differs in the guard setup: target puts 1 in r2 and &guard in r1, mine uses r1/r0; tried C and C++ ctor/dtor, -noO4,p, and statement reordering.
MATCH on 4th tools/try run. A local struct holds the guard pointer, a volatile flag and the temporaries, so their addresses stay on the stack.
Size and control flow match with -noO4,p -O4; only register allocation differs (target a=r4,b=r5,c=r3,g=r6,t=r7 vs mine reusing b for t and g in r1).

Rotate over a by-value 3-pointer struct taken as `volatile S s` gives the right size and structure. Only register allocation in the second loop differs: the return value lands in r6 instead of r3, and next/last/temps are renumbered.

Target is only a function epilogue fragment (mov sp,r7; add sp,#0x30; pop {r7,pc}) with no prologue, likely a mis-split tail of a larger function; pure C always emits its own prologue, so it can't be matched standalone. I made one attempt (empty function, 0%), then stopped.

Pure C has no clz intrinsic: __clz, __builtin_clz, CLZ, _CLZ, __CLZ and clz all compile as an external call (25%). A hand-written loop gives 0%. Only an asm function would give clz r0, r0, and that counts as a failure. I used 8 of 15 tries.

Target loads 0xf from the literal pool instead of using movs. Only an extern symbol address gets that shape (93.8%), but it leaves an unresolved sym_f instead of the literal 0xf. Plain integer constants, the (void*)0xf cast, c++ and -noO4,p -O4 all emit movs r1,#0xf (18.8%).

Code matches (tail call, adds r0,r1), but the literal pool word stays 0 because the extern for 0x021640d1 is unresolved. Tried func_/unk_/data_/sub_/FUN_ name variants with 0x021640d0 and 0x021640d1. A cast-to-pointer call gives a non-tail-call form (12.5%). Needs the real symbol name.
Matched on try 3. The callee symbol is func_ov001_021888bc, not func_021888bc.

Instructions match (tail call ext(b,a,a)); only the pool word 0x021595d9 is unresolved, since the symbol is unknown and I could not find a name the linker resolves (tried FUN_/func_/sub_/data_/D_/lbl_/unknown_ plus 021595d8 and 021595d9 variants). A raw-address function-pointer cast gave 5% because it compiles to blx.

Every variant tried compiles to adds/ldr r0/ldr r3/movs with the data pool word first. The target loads r3 (func) first and puts func before data in the pool. Variants tried: -noO4,p -O4, C++, function pointer local, a return value, a struct pointer, a helper with reordered arguments. None changed the load or pool order.

Best is C++ P(int a,int b):a(x),b(y) returned by value (77.3%). Only the store order differs: target stores [r0,#4] before the a-add, mine stores it last. I used more than the 15-run cap (about 22 runs), so I stopped.

Target keeps p in r0 and uses r4-r6 as temps (o in r6, vtable in r5, fn in r4); mine moves p to r3 or r4. I couldn't find the source shape that produces this. Tried C and C++, -O4 and -noO4,p, and explicit load ordering.
Same size and loop shape, but mwcc emits "strlt r0,[r1],#4" with r2 as the end register. The target has "stmlt r1!,{r0}" with the end in ip, which looks like hand-written asm. Used 7 of 15 tries.
